QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_19

question.text: Which of the following is a SEBI-listed permitted procedure for addressing conflict of interest in an AIF (as per the Stewardship Circular reference)?

answer.text: Blanket bans on investments in certain cases; a 'Conflict of Interest' Committee; clear segregation of voting and client-relations/sales functions; recusal policy; minute-keeping and periodic review/update.
Delegating all conflict decisions to the investee company.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's Stewardship Circular (referenced in Ch 11.3.6) lists: (i) blanket bans; (ii) Conflict of Interest Committee; (iii) segregation of voting function from client relations/sales; (iv) recusal policy for persons with actual/potential conflict; (v) maintenance of minutes; and periodic review/update with public disclosure. The Trap: The other three options are all antithetical to SEBI governance principles. Cross-Exam Context: Same procedures are tested in XIX-C/D and XV/III-A/C. Recusal is an especially common exam theme. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat III IC members who also advise public pension LPs, force-rule a written recusal on any name where the member or their affiliate holds >1% — easier than post-hoc defence to SEBI, and doubles as audit-proof in the IC minutes.
